problem_statement: When a sector's data area is completely packed with no erased space remaining for new data (e.g. after a power loss during the last ATE write at the sector end), nvs_mount() fails to mount the storage. Instead, such a sector should be treated as logically closed and mountable, with garbage collection triggered on the next write to restore a writable sector.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/subsys/fs/nvs -s tests/subsys/fs/nvs/filesystem.nvs -s filesystem.nvs -O twister-out --no-clean -W

verification.reason: The problem statement clearly describes the bug (nvs_mount fails when a sector's data area is completely packed after ATE power loss) and the expected behavior (the sector should be mountable and GC triggered on the next write). The hidden test checks exactly these behaviors—nvs_mount succeeding, nvs_write succeeding, and the write address moving to the other sector after GC—all of which a competent developer could infer from the statement. No new names, exact values, or implementation details are needed beyond what the statement provides.
